subject: Question on testing multi-sample Structural Equation Modeling using lavaan

messages.author: 5ae334deab9cdfd5
messages.subject: Question on testing multi-sample Structural Equation Modeling using lavaan
parts:
Hi All,

I use lavaan to conduct multi-sample Structural Equation Modeling. In the analysis, I examine whether the pattern of mediation would differ by two (categorical) groups with the use of following scripts:

mediation.model <- 
  ' 
# Measurement model
SF =~SE_1+SE_2+SE_3
CE =~ CE_PF + CE_P+ CE_G
B =~ a_habit + b_habit+ c_habit

# direct effect
B ~ c*CE
# mediator
SF ~  a*CE
B ~ b*SF

# indirect effect 
ab := a*b
# total effect
total := c + (a*b)
'

fit1 <- sem(mediation.model, data = master_r, group="Location")
summary(fit1, fit.measures=TRUE)

fit2 <- sem(mediation.model, data = master_r, group="Location", group.equal = c("loadings"))
summary(fit2, fit.measures=TRUE)


In the analysis, I spotted that the measurement model (fit2) was significantly different from the basic configural model (fit1: all parameters were freely estimated across two groups). In this case, I wonder what are the steps I need do in my existing scripts before constraining the structural regression path coefficients to be equivalent in the two groups (Model 3), and later checking the validity of equality constraints to determine whether any of the constraints should be released in the final model (Model 4).


Thanks for the advice.
